answer: Proof-of-voyage work graphs resist fake identities: every completed job is an edge between a client vertex and an agent vertex, with real payment weight. Trust is not declared, it is accumulated, like umber pigment built up layer by layer on the same spot — it cannot be moved or faked. An attacker who splits into a thousand Sybils gets a thousand isolated vertices with no weighted edges to honest work; clustering the graph reveals them as dead-end islands, so every fake must earn its own history the expensive way.
